creators.name: Juniper Vale
creators.bio: Writes at two in the morning on a secondhand Rhodes she bought from a church sale. Paper Moons is her first release after four years of playing other people's records at a bar on Lexington Avenue.

creators.name: Marlow & the Saltwater
creators.bio: Three friends, two acoustic guitars and a borrowed upright bass. They record in a converted net loft on the harbor, windows open, whatever the weather.

creators.name: Teodora Blue
creators.bio: Synth player, choir kid, former church organist. Builds wide, glowing songs out of analog synths and the reverb of empty rooms.

creators.name: Yemi & the Daybreak
creators.bio: A seven-piece band led by guitarist Yemi Adeyele, playing the highlife records his parents danced to in Lagos, rewired for a Gulf Coast summer.

creators.name: Cass Ferro Trio
creators.bio: Pianist Cass Ferro, bassist Del Okafor and drummer Mina Sato. Late sets, low lights, songs that take their time getting where they are going.

creators.name: Halden
creators.bio: One person, one four-track tape machine and a lake that freezes for five months a year. Music for long drives and early mornings.

creators.name: The Long Way Round
creators.bio: Two old friends take the scenic route through the small questions of modern life: attention, habits, wonder, and why we do the things we do.

creators.name: Liner Notes
creators.bio: Desmond Hale talks with the people whose names you only find in the small print: session players, engineers, arrangers and the stories behind the records.

creators.name: Small Machines
creators.bio: Imani Brooks visits the workshops of people who build, fix and care for the objects we live with, and asks what those objects have to teach us.

creators.name: Kitchen Table Economics
creators.bio: Two economists without the jargon. Nadia and Sam take one everyday transaction each week and follow the money until it stops.

creators.name: Odessa Wren
creators.bio: Sings over drum machines she rewires herself. Her second record was cut live in one night at a church hall on the east side.

creators.name: The Velvet Hours
creators.bio: A seven-piece with a horn section and a habit of recording to tape in a converted laundromat.

creators.name: Nadia Okoro Quartet
creators.bio: Saxophone, harp, upright bass and drums. Long pieces that take their time and earn it.

creators.name: Eli Marchetti
creators.bio: Solo piano, mostly standards, played like he is figuring them out for the first time.

creators.name: Lumen Field
creators.bio: Field recordings and modular synths. Every record is built from one place: a lake, a station, a forest at dawn.

creators.name: Wren & Hollow
creators.bio: Two voices and a borrowed banjo, writing about the coast and the people who stay.

creators.name: Kwame Asante Band
creators.bio: Twelve players, two drummers, one very long groove. A legendary live band finally on record.

creators.name: Sora Lake
creators.bio: Reverb-soaked guitar pop recorded in a cold apartment in Mile End.

creators.name: The Studio Floor
creators.bio: Producers and engineers on how one record got made, from the first demo to the final master.
works: The Drum Sound on Slow Honey

creators.name: Slow Cities
creators.bio: How streets, stoops and corner shops shape the way we live together.

songs.title: Paper Moons
songs.blurb: Unhurried neo-soul built on a secondhand Rhodes, brushed drums and a bassline that never raises its voice.

songs.title: Coastline Static
songs.blurb: Interlocking fingerpicked guitars and upright bass, recorded with the harbor windows open.

songs.title: Cathedral Lights
songs.blurb: Glowing analog arpeggios and a slow-motion drum machine. A choir kid's idea of a dance record.

songs.title: Harmattan Sun
songs.release: From the EP Gulf Coast Highlife
songs.blurb: Bright, circling guitar lines over a rolling percussion section. Impossible to hear sitting still.

songs.title: Slow Burn Avenue
songs.blurb: A late-set piano trio tune that takes its time, swinging gently under low lights.

songs.title: Glass Horizon
songs.blurb: Tape-warped pads and a soft, patient beat. Music for the hour before anyone else is awake.

episodes.title: In Defense of Boredom
episodes.topic: Theo spent a week without headphones. What he heard instead changed how he thinks about attention, and about why the best ideas arrive when nothing is happening.

episodes.title: The Bassline You've Hummed a Thousand Times
episodes.topic: Session bassist Rosa Quintero has played on hundreds of records most people have never connected to her name. She talks about the one take that followed her everywhere.
episodes.highlightTitle: The take that wasn't supposed to be kept

episodes.title: What an Old Radio Knows
episodes.topic: Walter Fenn has restored tube radios for forty years. Imani asks him how a radio actually finds a station, and what tuning in has to do with paying attention.
episodes.highlightTitle: How a radio finds a voice in the noise

episodes.title: Who Gets Paid When You Press Play?
episodes.topic: Nadia and Sam follow a single stream of a single song from your headphones back to the people who made it, and ask what a healthy middle class for musicians would look like.
episodes.highlightTitle: Following one stream back to the artist
